title: Redwood security/BCDR incident response & SLA review - ValleyTrust Bank
summary: High-level review of Redwood's incident response and BCDR processes. Customer focused on RTO/RPO guarantees, escalation paths, and auditability. Agreed to run a tabletop exercise and provide SOC 2 report + runbook links.
transcription:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Ethan Lewis (Redwood SE); Laura Chen (ValleyTrust CISO); Tom Alvarez (Head of Ops); Priya Rao (Sr Cloud Engineer)

00:00 Laura Chen: Okay we're on, thanks everyone for joining.
00:04 Maya Patel: Hey Laura, thanks for making the time. I'll kick off quick, today's goal is to walk through our incident response and BCDR (sorry B-C-D-R), RTO/RPO commitments, and the escalation chain — make sure it aligns with ValleyTrust's controls.
00:14 Tom Alvarez: Yep, and Laura asked me to double-check the SLA items — uptime, maintenance windows, and how alerts are routed to our on-call.
00:21 Ethan Lewis: I'll cover technical pieces — runbooks, failover behaviour, backup cadence, and how our platform integrates with customer KMS for key management.
00:28 Laura Chen: Great. A couple context points: we're regulated, need data residency in us-east-1 today, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 are must haves for procurement, and we use Okta SSO + SCIM for provisioning.
00:38 Maya Patel: Totally. Redwood supports SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC with custom roles, and we can restrict admin actions — we'll show some examples.
00:45 Priya Rao: Quick question before we dive in — for encryption, are customer keys hosted in our KMS or in vendor-managed? Our policy requires customer-managed keys if possible.
00:55 Ethan Lewis: Good q. We offer both: customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integration and Redwood-managed keys. With customer KMS, data at rest encryption uses your KMS wrap keys; we never persist raw keys. There's also envelope encryption and logging of key usage in audit logs.
01:10 Tom Alvarez: How granular are audit logs? We need tamper-evident logs for actions like key rotations, admin role changes, and model access requests.
01:18 Ethan Lewis: Audit logs include API calls, console actions, admin changes, and key usage events. Logs are write-once in our log storage and can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging sinks; TTL can be configured per contract.
01:32 Laura Chen: And for IR, what are your RTO and RPO numbers? We need specifics for incident classification — CRITICAL vs HIGH vs MEDIUM.
01:40 Maya Patel: For hosted customers we commit to 99.95% uptime in our standard SLA with different credits; for Dedicated/Private we can negotiate stricter SLOs — for incident response we have published RTO targets: critical incidents — aim to restore service within 2 hours, RPO for critical is near-zero (<1 minute) for core control plane state via active replication. For non-critical, longer windows.
01:59 Tom Alvarez: 2 hours RTO for critical is reasonable but how often is that hit? What's your MTTR historically?
02:05 Ethan Lewis: Historically our MTTR for critical incidents has been around 35-90 minutes, depending on root cause. We run game days and we have post-incident reviews; we share redacted postmortems under NDA for customers.
02:18 Laura Chen: Postmortems under NDA is good. For BCDR, if an entire region fails (say us-east-1), what is the failover path? Are you multi-region active-active or active-passive?
02:28 Ethan Lewis: Our architecture supports active-active routing across regions for stateless endpoints; for stateful artifacts we replicate across regions asynchronously with a cross-region KV cache replication. For strict RPO/RTO for Dedicated customers we can enable synchronous replication modes. For hosted, by default we have warm-standby in a secondary region with automated DNS failover — the RTO there is target 30-60 minutes depending on DNS propagation and cache warming.
02:48 Priya Rao: That DNS step worries me — we have clients that need sub-5 minute failovers.
02:53 Maya Patel: For sub-5 minute requirements, we recommend Dedicated with regional failover and BGP-level routing or using our private deployment in your VPC. We can set up BGP/anycast routes for faster cutover.
03:06 Tom Alvarez: Okay makes sense. On escalation: who do we call for a 24/7 critical incident? Is there a pager or an on-call roster?
03:12 Ethan Lewis: We have a 24/7 on-call rotation in SRE; primary pager is our SRE duty team, then escalation to SRE leads, then to engineering managers. For enterprise contracts we provide a named escalation contact with direct dial and a war room Slack channel.
03:26 Laura Chen: Can we get a runbook example and the contact matrix?
03:30 Maya Patel: Yes, we'll share a redacted runbook and a sample contact matrix. We'll also include escalation SLAs — time to respond, time to acknowledge, next escalation step.
03:38 Tom Alvarez: For legal/procurement, what about data residency and backups? Are backups stored in same region? How long retained?
03:45 Ethan Lewis: Backups are by default stored in the same region and encrypted with your KMS keys. Retention configurable — standard 30 days, add-ons for 1 year+ for compliance. We can set snapshots to be geo-redundant if required, but that'll affect RPO.
03:58 Laura Chen: And for audits: do you provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation?
04:03 Maya Patel: We provide SOC 2 Type II reports to customers under NDA and have ISO 27001 cert. We'll send both docs after the call.
04:09 Priya Rao: When you forward logs to our SIEM, is there guaranteed ordering and integrity? We need to correlate events across systems.
04:16 Ethan Lewis: Logs include sequence numbers and are sent with checksums; we support CloudTrail-style events and can ship via secure channels. For long-term archival we can send to your S3 with object locking if you need immutable retention.
04:30 Laura Chen: Great. One more: in an incident where a vulnerability was found in a third-party library affecting inference, what's your disclosure process and timeline?
04:38 Ethan Lewis: We have coordinated disclosure policies: emergency patch within 48 hours for critical CVEs, notify affected customers within 24 hours of impact assessment, and provide mitigation steps. We also push hotfixes to Dedicated clusters with scheduled maintenance windows unless emergency.
04:54 Tom Alvarez: Sounds reasonable.
04:57 Maya Patel: Ok let's run a quick tabletop scenario — region outage affecting model serving; how would ValleyTrust want notification and what are your RTO targets internally?
05:06 Laura Chen: We want immediate PagerDuty alerts and a high-severity incident opened; RTO target 1 hour for critical services, but we can be flexible if we have deterministic failover steps.
05:16 Ethan Lewis: Noted. On the technical side, our KV cache priming is the longest piece — warming can take up to 20-30 minutes; we can pre-warm critical prefixes if you provide expected traffic patterns.
05:30 Priya Rao: Can we see metrics around cache warmup and request tail latency during failover?
05:34 Ethan Lewis: Yes, we can share dashboards with p50/p95/p99 latencies and cache hit rates; those are available via Redwood Console or can be exported to your monitoring stack.
05:46 Laura Chen: For the SLA credits, what's the formula? We need it in the contract.
05:51 Maya Patel: Our standard formula: credits scale with downtime percentage per calendar month; for example 99.95% guarantees 22 minutes of downtime per month; credits tiered (10% credit for first tier, more for higher breaches). We will send the SLA doc with exact math.
06:05 Tom Alvarez: Circle back on compliance checks — do you do annual pen tests and internal audits?
06:10 Ethan Lewis: Yes we have annual third-party pen tests and internal red team exercises; summaries available redacted for customers. We also maintain a vulnerability tracking dashboard.
06:20 Laura Chen: Thanks. Let's confirm next steps and action items.
06:24 Maya Patel: Quick recap: we'll send SOC2 and ISO certs, redacted runbook, sample contact matrix, SLA doc, and a proposal for a tabletop game day. We'll also provide a dedicated trial cluster for performance/BCDR validation.
06:35 Tom Alvarez: Can we get a timeline? We need this before procurement cycle end — two weeks.
06:40 Maya Patel: We'll aim to deliver docs in 3 business days and propose tabletop dates next week. Trial cluster can be provisioned within 5 business days once NDA and contract terms are in motion.
06:50 Laura Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everybody.
06:52 Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email. Bye.
